title: Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 5 – Earth’s Processes
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Earth and Environmental Science Module 5, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
course: NSW Earth and Environmental Science Stage 6
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How did today’s biosphere originate and develop?

questions.prompt: What experiment produced organic molecules from gases thought to resemble early Earth’s atmosphere?
What simple organic molecules were produced in the Miller–Urey experiment?
What deep-ocean hydrothermal features are proposed as possible sites for early life?
What hypothesis proposes that life or its building blocks arrived on Earth from space?
What photosynthetic microorganisms formed ancient stromatolites?
What event marks a rapid diversification of animal life early in the Phanerozoic?

categories.name: How did the biosphere change Earth’s other spheres?

questions.prompt: What gas released by early photosynthetic organisms accumulated in Earth’s atmosphere?
What layered iron-rich rocks formed when oxygen reacted with dissolved iron in ancient oceans?
What atmospheric layer formed from oxygen and helped shield life from ultraviolet radiation?
Which sphere contains Earth’s liquid water and oceans?
Which sphere includes rocks, minerals and the solid Earth?
The spread of photosynthesis caused atmospheric carbon dioxide to generally increase or decrease over long timescales?

categories.name: What effect does the plate tectonic supercycle have?

questions.prompt: What term describes a huge landmass formed when most continents join together?
What supercontinent existed late in the Palaeozoic and early Mesozoic?
What process begins the breakup of a supercontinent as continental crust pulls apart?
What mountain-building process commonly occurs when continents collide?
What broad cycle describes repeated assembly and breakup of supercontinents?
questions.answer: The plate tectonic supercycle. Accept: supercontinent cycle.

questions.prompt: Changes in continental positions can alter ocean circulation and therefore affect what major Earth system?

categories.name: What do fossils reveal about geological time and past life?

questions.prompt: What preserved remains or traces of past organisms are called?
What fossil forms when an organism leaves an impression in sediment that later hardens?
What fossil forms when a mould is later filled with minerals or sediment?
What fossils such as footprints or burrows record the activity of organisms?
What type of fossil is especially useful for correlating and dating rock layers over large areas?
What principle states that in an undisturbed sequence, older sedimentary layers lie below younger layers?
questions.answer: The principle of superposition. Accept: superposition.

finalRound.prompt: What principle assumes that geological processes operating today also operated in the past?
